page: Amazon Web Services r6a.24xlarge is a memory-optimized cloud server instance powered by dedicated AMD EPYC 7R13 processors running on the AWS Nitro System hypervisor. Built on the x86_64 architecture, this instance supplies 48 physical cores and 96 virtual CPUs operating at clock frequencies up to 3.6 GHz. Memory capacity totals 768.0 GB of DDR4 RAM running at 3 GHz, which maintains a memory-to-vCPU allocation of 8.0 GB per core. The instance includes a 38 Gbps baseline network bandwidth configuration, contains zero GPUs, and includes no bundled local NVMe storage, requiring network-attached storage volumes for persistent data.

Benchmark results demonstrate superior parallel computational capacity and cryptographic efficiency. In multi-threaded evaluation, stress-ng multi-core CPU testing and PassMark CPU encryption tests place the instance in the top 10 percent tier. The system also registers strong top-quartile results in PassMark overall CPU benchmarks, PassMark database operations, and Redis SET throughput reaching 92.53 million operations per second. Conversely, single-core metrics such as Geekbench single-core and uncached 256MB block memory bandwidth tests position within the middle 50 percent distribution, highlighting that high throughput is tied directly to distributed parallel thread saturation rather than isolated single-thread speeds.

The hardware configuration provides favorable resource density for organizations requiring substantial memory capacity combined with high multi-threaded compute. Because persistent local disks are absent, architectural planning must factor in external EBS network-attached storage integration. Given the 1:8 vCPU-to-memory ratio, large DDR4 footprint, and 38 Gbps baseline network throughput, the r6a.24xlarge is well tailored for enterprise in-memory caching layers, massive relational or NoSQL database clusters, distributed data analytics pipelines, and large-scale ETL processing.
description: Amazon Web Services r6a.24xlarge is an enterprise-grade memory-optimized instance featuring 96 vCPUs and 48 physical cores powered by AMD EPYC 7R13 processors at 3.6 GHz. Built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor with x86_64 architecture, it delivers 768.0 GB of DDR4 memory across an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio, backed by 38 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. The instance bundles no local disk storage and includes no discrete graphics processing units. Synthetic and real-world benchmarks show top-tier multi-threaded CPU stress throughput and cryptographic processing, alongside top-quartile PassMark database scores and Redis key-value operations reaching 92.53 million transactions per second. Lacking local storage, it relies on network volumes for persistent storage. The r6a.24xlarge delivers cost-efficient scale for in-memory databases, real-time caching fleets, and high-concurrency analytical engines.
